topic: Know your customer and data protection
title: Onboarding a customer by the book
instructions:
## You design the onboarding flow for a fintech app

The product team wants sign-up in under two minutes. Compliance wants KYC done properly and personal data handled lawfully. Make the decisions that satisfy both.

nodes.title: Identity
nodes.text: Which identity check meets the KYC requirement for a full wallet in Ghana?

choices.text: Verify the Ghana Card number and details against the national identity register, with a liveness check of the selfie
choices.feedback: Correct. Verification against an authoritative source, not just a photo of a card.

choices.text: Ask the user to type their name and date of birth
Skip identity for small wallets forever
choices.feedback: Tiered limits can lower the burden for small wallets, but full wallets need verification.

nodes.title: Tiering
nodes.text: A market trader wants to start quickly and has no document on her. What is the lawful, usable path?

choices.text: A tier-1 wallet with low limits on a phone number, upgraded when her ID is verified
choices.feedback: Correct. Risk-based tiers are how regulators balance inclusion and control.
Financial inclusion is a regulatory goal too.

choices.text: Give her a full wallet and verify later
choices.feedback: Full limits without verification defeat the control.

nodes.title: Data minimisation
nodes.text: The product team wants to collect contacts, location history and photos at sign-up "for future features". Under the Data Protection Act this is:

choices.text: Not allowed: collect only what the stated purpose needs, and ask again when a new purpose arises
choices.feedback: Correct. Purpose limitation and data minimisation are core principles.

choices.text: Fine if buried in the terms
choices.feedback: Consent must be specific and informed.

choices.text: Fine because the data stays in Ghana
choices.feedback: Location of storage does not justify over-collection.

nodes.title: Retention
nodes.text: How long should KYC records be kept after an account closes?

choices.text: For the period the regulation requires, then deleted or anonymised
choices.feedback: Correct. Retention follows the legal requirement, no shorter and no longer.
Regulations require records for a set period.

nodes.title: Automation
nodes.text: Compliance currently checks every sign-up by hand and takes a day. What does RegTech change?

choices.text: Automated verification and rule checks with human review only for exceptions, and an audit trail of every decision
choices.feedback: Correct. Automate the routine, keep people for the edge cases, and log everything for the regulator.
The obligation does not go away; its execution changes.

nodes.title: Flow approved
nodes.text: Verified identity for full wallets, tiered limits for quick starts, minimal data, lawful retention and automated checks with an audit trail.

hints: Tiered wallets balance inclusion and control.
Collect only what the stated purpose needs.

checks.label: At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: Bank of Ghana's tiered KYC for e-money and the Data Protection Act 843 are the two frameworks this flow has to satisfy at once; RegTech vendors sell exactly this combination.
